steps.label: 🔥 FROM BACKEND 🔥
steps.description: The browser parses the URL, checks its cache, and prepares to reach out to the server. It resolves the hostname to begin establishing a connection.

steps.label: DNS Lookup
steps.description: The browser asks a DNS resolver to translate the hostname (e.g. example.com) into an IP address. The resolver may query root, TLD, and authoritative name servers before returning a result.

steps.label: TCP Handshake
steps.description: A reliable connection is established using the three-way TCP handshake: the browser sends SYN, the server replies SYN-ACK, and the browser confirms with ACK. Both sides are now in sync.

steps.label: TLS Handshake
steps.description: The browser and server negotiate a cipher suite, exchange certificates, and establish shared encryption keys. All subsequent traffic will be encrypted — this is what turns HTTP into HTTPS.

steps.label: HTTP Request
steps.description: The browser sends an encrypted HTTP request (e.g. GET /) over the established secure channel. Headers like Host, Accept, and cookies travel with the request.

steps.label: HTTP Response
steps.description: The server processes the request and sends back an encrypted HTTP response — typically 200 OK with the HTML, CSS, and JS the browser needs to render the page.
